items.title: 68252_Jay Cee
items.q: INTERVIEWER: '...somebody like Alberta Hunter really made the Book on Jazz.' INTERVIEWEE: 'Well, that's ordinary...'

ctx.x: Sure. Sure. All right. Now, why -- we

looked in the books. I mean I've talked to you about going through 20, 30 books, and there is so little reference, maybe a word here on Helen Humes. Now, yet somebody like Alberta Hunter really made the Book on Jazz. And Helen Humes was omitted. Now, what do you think -- how does something like that happen?
Well, that's ordinary. Some people get more publicity than that -- they get the right publicity at the right time and the right place (inaudible). But that's easy to understand.

items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: I was singing that for J.C. Johnson, and I tried to do a good job

ctx.x: Oh, no. My mother was a little against that. And then when I would sing "My Particular Man," I was singing that for J.C. Johnson, and I tried to do a good job, so inasmuch as the song was being sung, I wanted to sing it so that he could make the money.
